subject: biology

concepts.title: Endocrine Glands and Hormones
concepts.definition: Chemical substances that function as messengers between cells, are not used as nutrients, and are synthesized in minute quantities by ductless glands.
concepts.key_idea: Hormones provide a slow but long-lasting coordination system compared to the rapid neural system.
question_patterns: define a hormone according to the modern scientific view
how do endocrine glands differ from exocrine glands
what are the characteristics of hormones
explain why hormones are called intercellular messengers
short note on endocrine glands and hormones

solution_steps.explain: Endocrine glands lack ducts and release secretions directly into the blood.
Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals produced in trace amounts.
Verify that hormonal coordination is slower but longer-lasting compared to the rapid neural coordination via nerve impulses.

concepts.title: The Hypothalamus
concepts.definition: The basal part of the forebrain that contains neurosecretory cells which form hormones to regulate the pituitary gland.
concepts.key_idea: The hypothalamus links the nervous system to the endocrine system via releasing and inhibiting hormones.
question_patterns: what is the role of the hypothalamus in the endocrine system
distinguish between releasing and inhibiting hormones
how does the hypothalamus control the anterior pituitary
name a hormone that inhibits growth hormone release
describe the hypothalamus with an example

solution_steps.explain: Hypothalamic nuclei produce neurohormones.
Hormones reach the anterior pituitary through a portal circulatory system.
Verify that releasing hormones stimulate pituitary secretion while inhibiting hormones such as somatostatin suppress it.

concepts.title: The Pituitary Gland and Growth Disorders
concepts.definition: A master gland located in the sella tursica that secretes several trophic hormones and stores hypothalamic hormones.
concepts.key_idea: The pituitary regulates growth, milk production, and the activity of other endocrine glands.
question_patterns: what causes gigantism and dwarfism
list the hormones of the anterior pituitary
what is the function of oxytocin and vasopressin
describe the condition called acromegaly
what do you understand by the pituitary gland and growth disorders

solution_steps.explain: Growth Hormone (GH) regulates body development.
Over-secretion leads to gigantism/acromegaly; under-secretion leads to dwarfism.
Verify that oxytocin causes uterine contraction during childbirth and vasopressin regulates water reabsorption in the kidneys.

concepts.title: Thyroid Gland and Metabolism
concepts.definition: A two-lobed gland in the neck that produces thyroxine and triiodothyronine to regulate the body's basal metabolic rate.
concepts.key_idea: Iodine is necessary for thyroid hormone synthesis, which controls nutrient metabolism and RBC formation.
question_patterns: why is iodine important in our diet
what are the symptoms of hypothyroidism during pregnancy
explain the role of thyrocalcitonin
what is Graves' disease
state two key points about thyroid gland and metabolism

solution_steps.explain: Iodine is needed for T3 and T4 synthesis.
Deficiency causes goitre and cretinism; excess causes hyperthyroidism.
Confirm that thyroid follicles also secrete thyrocalcitonin which lowers blood calcium levels, acting antagonistically to parathyroid hormone.

concepts.title: Parathyroid Gland and Calcium Balance
concepts.definition: Four small glands on the thyroid's back that secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH) to increase blood calcium levels.
concepts.key_idea: PTH and TCT act antagonistically to maintain calcium homeostasis in the blood.
question_patterns: how does PTH increase blood calcium levels
why is PTH called a hypercalcemic hormone
name the hormone that regulates calcium along with PTH
where does PTH act to increase calcium
list the main features of parathyroid gland and calcium balance

solution_steps.explain: Low circulating blood calcium levels trigger PTH secretion.
PTH stimulates bone resorption and renal calcium reabsorption.
Confirm that PTH raises blood calcium while thyroid-derived thyrocalcitonin lowers it, maintaining calcium homeostasis.

concepts.title: Adrenal Gland and Stress Response
concepts.definition: Glands located above the kidneys consisting of a medulla (secreting emergency hormones) and a cortex (secreting corticoids).
concepts.key_idea: The adrenal gland manages both immediate stress (medulla) and long-term metabolic/electrolyte balance (cortex).
question_patterns: what are the hormones of fight or flight
explain the function of aldosterone
what is Addison's disease
how does cortisol affect the immune system
short note on adrenal gland and stress response

solution_steps.explain: Adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline; cortex secretes cortisol and aldosterone.
Adrenaline increases heart rate; aldosterone regulates sodium and water balance.
Verify that underproduction of glucocorticoids causes Addison's disease while overproduction causes Cushing's syndrome.

concepts.title: Pancreas and Glucose Homeostasis
concepts.definition: A composite gland containing Islets of Langerhans that secrete insulin and glucagon to manage blood sugar.
concepts.key_idea: Insulin (hypoglycemic) and glucagon (hyperglycemic) maintain stable blood glucose levels.
question_patterns: how do insulin and glucagon regulate blood sugar
what is the cause of diabetes mellitus
which cells secrete insulin
define hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia
justify why pancreas and glucose homeostasis matters

solution_steps.explain: Alpha cells secrete glucagon; Beta cells secrete insulin.
Insulin promotes glucose uptake; glucagon promotes glycogen breakdown.
Verify that insufficient insulin secretion causes diabetes mellitus, characterized by elevated blood glucose and glucose loss in urine.

concepts.title: Mechanism of Hormone Action
concepts.definition: The process where hormones bind to specific receptors to trigger biochemical changes and physiological responses in target tissues.
concepts.key_idea: Water-soluble hormones use second messengers, while lipid-soluble hormones regulate gene expression directly.
question_patterns: how do protein hormones differ from steroid hormones in action
what are second messengers in hormone action
explain the formation of a hormone-receptor complex
where are intracellular receptors located
explain mechanism of hormone action in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the hormone is peptide-based or steroid-based.
Peptides bind to membrane receptors; steroids bind to intracellular receptors.
Verify that peptide hormones generate second messengers such as cyclic AMP while steroid hormones directly regulate gene expression by binding to nuclear receptors.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A patient has high blood sugar and glucose in their urine. Identify the likely disorder and the hormone deficiency.

solution_template.explain: High blood sugar (hyperglycemia) and glucosuria are key indicators.
The disorder is caused by a deficiency of insulin.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Which gland is responsible for maintaining the sleep-wake cycle and what hormone does it secrete?

solution_template.explain: The 24-hour diurnal rhythm includes the sleep-wake cycle.
The pineal gland, located on the dorsal side of the forebrain, regulates this.
